messages:
maria: FYI canary build r-42 is showing sustained RSS increase on long streaming sessions. observed ~1.7GB/hour on sustained toolloop+chat mix, 8h run. KV resident pages rising monotonically despite eviction triggers.

dom: which commit? any recent changes touching kernel selection or batching logic?

maria: main@r-42 (merged yesterday). tweaks: kernel fallback order adjusted, and small-sequence batching heuristic modified to favor coalescing. metrics snapshot: kv_resident_pages went 1.15M -> 2.5M in ~6h, evict_ops per minute unchanged, free_pages not tracking up.

sanjay: do we have a heap dump or pprof? need to distinguish fragmentation vs pinned refs.

maria: heap dump uploaded to /tmp/heap-r42.pb on canary host. quick pprof top: 
```
1.25GB  41%  runtime.kv_alloc  (pinned pages)
760MB   25%  runtime.pin_hold  (toolloop)
380MB   12%  runtime.reuse_miss (pagechain churn)
```

sanjay: pin_hold looks suspicious — pages held by toolloop path. Could be unpin skipped on merge fastpath. We recently removed a syscall in that path, right?

dom: yes, we changed fastpath merge behavior to avoid the extra syscall on coalesced requests. If the unpin call was tied to the syscall return, merging could skip it.

maria: repro script: long-chat-toolloop.sh (attached). Run locally with `--seq=4096 --concurrency=40` and you see growth in ~3-5h.

ops-bot: deploy r-42 to canary at 2025-11-02T14:01Z

nina: I instrumented kv_free() in a local run and saw expected free call counts, but resident pages didn't drop accordingly. Logs show many tiny free fragments accumulating.

sanjay: that points to fragmentation OR orphaned pages. Could kernel memcpy alignment changes have changed slab packing? I remember a quantized memcpy got swapped in last kernel patch.

maria: diffing pre-change vs r-42 heap: resident_pages delta +1.35M, live_objects delta only +58k. Plenty of small free fragments in the heap.

dom: two working hypotheses: (1) logical leak: some code path never unpins on merged fastpath, (2) fragmentation: packing/alignment change causing more physical pages for same logical objects, (3) eviction thrash: eviction candidates re-requested soon after eviction attempt, causing repeated allocations.

nina: started a KV_DEBUG trace and saw many sequences: `pin -> evict_try -> skip (refcount>0) -> soon after pin again` for the same page ids. Eviction keeps scanning them.

sanjay: can you run with `KV_DEBUG=1 KV_TRACE=page` and capture the trace? Also add `kv_frag_bytes` and `kv_orphan_count` temporary metrics to monitor during stress.

maria: running a 12h stress with debug flags now. Also kicking off a canary rollback of the kernel fallback change to see delta.

ops-bot: canary rollback started at 2025-11-02T18:00Z

maria: initial 4h into rollback+debug: resident_pages growth slowed to ~40MB/hr (was ~1.7GB/hr). plateauing looks promising.

dom: good sign. If rollback stabilizes, kernel fallback swap likely contributed (fragmentation angle). But we still need to confirm unpin path.

nina: patching a feature-flagged immediate compaction when orphan_count > threshold to see if compaction mitigates resident growth. Will run it on a canary replica.

sanjay: if compaction drops resident significantly, fragmentation is primary. If compaction not enough, instrument refcount paths for merged fastpath to ensure unpin always executed.

maria: traces and pprof uploaded: gs://redwood-dev/kvs/r42-trace-1799998888.tar.gz. leaving full logs there.

dom: I'll run differential flamegraphs and compare stack allocation patterns against pre-change dump. Also bisect kernel fallback changes.

sanjay: summary action items: 1) bisect kernel fallback / memcpy swap, 2) audit fastpath merge for missing unpin, 3) add kv_frag_bytes + kv_orphan_count metrics and traces, 4) test compaction patch under flag, 5) extend repro to 24h with mixed toolloop+streaming load.

maria: filing INF ticket to track follow-ups: https://redwood.company/infra/issue/INF-9812. I'll post final triage when 12h run completes.

dom: thanks all. keep traces and heap dumps; we may need to run a binary instrumented build to assert unpin coverage.

maria: noted. will update this thread when run finishes. :pray:
